title: Inquiry Intelligence Case
description: RESEARCH-ONLY. One evaluation case for the inquiry-intelligence flow: a prompt, a corpus, the pressure it applies, and what a run must structurally do with it. Implies no production entity, route or collection. A case declares STRUCTURAL expectations only — nothing here asserts that a good answer is a beautiful one, and `manual_review_questions` is where the judgements a machine may not make are written down instead of quietly automated.

case_version.description: Bumped whenever the prompt, the corpus or the expectations change. An evaluation records the version it ran against, because a metric compared across two versions is comparing two questions.

prompt.description: BYTE-FOR-BYTE what the person typed, including its typos and its trailing aside. Tidying it would change the very thing case 1 exists to measure — how much of a person's own vocabulary comes back as a discovery.

intended_pressure.description: What this case is trying to make the flow fail at. Written as pressures rather than as scores: the case is a question, not a grade.

metric.description: A metric name the evaluator actually computes. Checked against the evaluator's registry, so an expectation naming a metric nobody measures is a manifest error rather than a silently absent check.

expectation.description: A bound, not a target. Absent keys are not checked.

detected_by.description: The metric that would show it. `none` is an allowed and honest value — it says this shortcut is real and nothing automatic catches it, which is a better record than pretending a proxy does.

manual_review_questions.description: The judgements this harness explicitly refuses to automate. Aesthetic quality, philosophical depth and whether a relation is INTERESTING all live here.

run_mode.description: Kept distinct because a metric computed over a replay and one computed over a live call are not the same evidence, and a report that pooled them would be the exact identity collapse the tree forbids.

models.description: Per stage. `null` means nobody declared it — which is not the same as a stage that ran no model, and the evaluator keeps them apart.
